quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: At a stop sign, you should stop and:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for tailgating cars.
Move when the car ahead moves.
Look right, then left, then right again.
Look left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left first because traffic from the left is closer to you. Then look right, then look left again to catch any vehicles you may have missed.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers turning left at a green light to yield to oncoming traffic. You can complete the turn when it is safe.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.
Keep tires at the correct air pressure.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when your car slides on water between the tires and road. Low tire pressure, worn tread, and speeding all increase hydroplaning risk.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Drive the same way as on dry roads.

questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase your distance from the car ahead. Your car will need more time to stop.

questions.question: Orange signs are:
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn that workers are on or near the highway. They are diamond-shaped with black letters or symbols.

questions.question: When driving in bad weather, drivers should:

options.text: Speed up to reach their destination faster.

questions.explanation: On wet roads, increase your distance from the car ahead.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is false?

options.text: Winter is the hardest driving season.
Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid in winter.
Cruise control is safe to use in winter weather.
Snow tires help your vehicle grip icy roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cruise control is safe to use in winter weather.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other hazardous conditions. Winter requires extra caution. Check antifreeze and washer fluid levels regularly. Snow tires improve traction on slippery roads.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickly when they are:
questions.explanation: Shaded areas under trees or buildings freeze first and dry last. Be extra careful on these sections of road in cold or wet weather.

questions.question: You are in the right lane on an expressway. Move to the left lane when:

options.text: Traffic is heavy but moving steadily.
Roads are slippery and weather is bad.
Your lane is slow and cars are in the left lane.
Traffic is light and cars are entering from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is light and cars are entering from the right.
questions.explanation: Watch for merging traffic on expressways. Move to another lane or adjust your speed so other drivers can merge safely.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that a four-way intersection is coming.

questions.question: Where is the best place to keep a space cushion?

options.text: Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space around all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to hazards. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your left and right sides.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
Honk your horn before passing on the left.
Keep driving when you think the children are done getting off.
Pass the bus before the door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when a school bus has its stop arm extended. Do not move until the stop arm is pulled in.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A series of curves is ahead.
The road will be slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will be slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road becomes especially slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass other vehicles from your direction.

questions.question: What should you do if another driver is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is open.
If no right lane is open, slow down gradually once the road ahead is clear. This helps the tailgater pass you.

questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you and a right lane is open, move over. If no right lane exists, slow down gradually once the road ahead is clear to let them pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of being hit from behind.

questions.question: What shape is a stop sign?
questions.explanation: Stop signs are eight-sided. All octagonal signs mean you must come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?

options.text: When road or weather conditions are not ideal.
When you see a police car.
When entering a highway with other cars.
When you are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: When road or weather conditions are not ideal.
questions.explanation: Drive below the posted speed limit when the road is wet or slippery, when you cannot see well, or when any other condition is not perfect. You can receive a ticket for driving too fast for conditions even if you are at the speed limit.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at the same time to a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: One driver may continue without stopping.
One driver should honk to show they are giving up the right-of-way.

questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, if both drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on your right has the right-of-way. You may proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn of hazards ahead. This sign tells drivers to be careful because wet pavement makes the road slippery and harder to control.

questions.question: What does it mean when a driver extends their left arm downward?
questions.explanation: When a driver extends their left arm downward, they are signaling that they plan to stop. Adjust your driving if you are following a vehicle using this hand signal.

questions.question: In normal weather and traffic, what is the minimum following distance you should keep?
questions.explanation: Keep three to four seconds between your car and the car ahead in normal conditions. This gives you time to react to hazards. In bad weather or heavy traffic, increase this distance.

questions.question: What should you do if another car is about to hit you?
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who might not see you. Sound your horn if you think another driver might hit you.

questions.question: When can you drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public highway?

options.text: As long as you aren't driving.
If you are riding in the back seat.
If you are riding in the back of a pick-up truck.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or carry open alcohol in a vehicle on any public road. This applies to all passengers and all areas of the vehicle.

questions.question: You have a green light and want to turn left, but traffic coming toward you is heavy. What should you do?

options.text: Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Go ahead since you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: When you have a green light, you can enter the intersection to turn left. Wait in the center for oncoming traffic to pass before you complete your turn.

questions.question: What does an orange sign mean?

options.text: The start of a no passing zone.

questions.explanation: Orange signs with black symbols warn about construction, maintenance, and emergency work.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road curves only to the right.
The road turns sharply to the right.
The road curves right, then left.
The road curves left, then right.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers the road ahead curves to the right and then to the left.

questions.question: What does a green arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: It is used only on one-way streets.
You may go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
You may only proceed if a circular green light is also showing.
It points the way to an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you have a protected turn. Traffic in that lane must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: How can you avoid the dangers of drinking and driving?

options.text: Decide before drinking that you won't drive.
Tell others "No thanks, I'm driving" if they offer you a drink.

questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drinking and driving is to decide before you drink that you won't drive. Alcohol affects your judgment, making it hard to make safe choices after you've started drinking.

questions.question: What helps drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Sitting in the driveway with the engine running.

questions.explanation: Quick stops waste fuel because you must accelerate again. Drivers who plan ahead can slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid sudden braking, which saves gas.

questions.question: What must you do when you come to a flashing red light?

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully through.
Turn right or left because the road ahead is blocked.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop completely. Proceed only when the way is clear.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic signal mean?

options.text: Proceed with caution at an intersection.

questions.explanation: A flashing red signal means stop. You must stop and let all other traffic pass before you go.

questions.question: What is the correct way to change lanes?

options.text: Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, look over your shoulder for blind spots, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, look over your shoulder for blind spots, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal first. Check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to see your blind spot. Make sure no one is moving into the same lane. Then change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do if your tire blows out?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not use your brakes right away.
Slowly reduce speed and pull to the side of the road.

questions.explanation: If your tire blows out, release the gas pedal and do not brake immediately. Slowly reduce your speed, then gently apply the brakes and move to the side of the road.

questions.question: What does a slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
questions.explanation: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles with this emblem drive at 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: Why is it important to keep space between your vehicle and others?

options.text: It reduces distractions from other drivers.
It gives you time to react to emergencies.
It keeps traffic moving at safe speeds.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react to emergencies.
questions.explanation: Space between vehicles gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: Who must wear a seat belt?
questions.explanation: The driver, front seat passengers, and all children under 16 must wear seat belts. A police officer can stop your vehicle if anyone is not buckled in.

questions.question: When can you exceed the speed limit?

options.text: When there are no police officers around.

questions.explanation: You may never exceed the speed limit. Always follow the posted speed limit.

questions.question: What is the "No zone"?

options.text: Areas around trucks and buses where drivers cannot see your car.
A road where stereo volume is restricted.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas around trucks and buses where drivers cannot see your car.
questions.explanation: Large trucks and buses have blind spots on both sides, in front, and in back. Your car cannot be seen in these areas. These areas are called the "No zone."

questions.question: When should you slow down when exiting a freeway?

options.text: After you move onto the exit ramp.
Keep your speed the same on the exit ramp.
Pass slower traffic in the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move onto the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Keep your freeway speed until you move onto the exit ramp. Then slow down.

questions.question: What should you do at dusk or on overcast days?

options.text: Do not turn on any lights.

questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dusk and on overcast days. Use low beams when within 1,000 feet of an oncoming vehicle or within 500 feet of a vehicle you are following. Always use low beams in bad weather.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow down gradually.
Turn on your hazard lights and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow down gradually.
questions.explanation: Do not brake suddenly when a tire blows out. Grip the steering wheel tightly and stay in your lane. Release the gas pedal and let your car slow down. Once you are moving slowly, gently apply the brakes and pull off the road to a safe spot.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a steep hill ahead.
Trucks are not allowed on the hill ahead.
Trucks are on the hill ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep hill or downgrade is coming.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a low ground railroad crossing. Railroad tracks cross the road at a steep angle. The bottom of low vehicles may scrape or get stuck on the tracks.

questions.question: Why should drivers be extra alert to motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians?

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic.
They follow different traffic laws than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers looked but did not see motorcycles, bicycles, or pedestrians. These are harder to spot because they are smaller and have less noticeable lights. Stay alert to prevent crashes with these road users.

questions.question: How can you make sure your physical condition does not cause unsafe driving?

options.text: Stay physically fit and get regular check-ups.
Know how any medicine affects your driving.

questions.explanation: Your physical health affects your ability to drive safely. Know your limits and only drive when it is safe.

questions.question: You are driving at night and another vehicle is coming toward you. Your headlights should be:

options.text: Off. Use your parking lights instead.
On high beam or low beam—either is fine.

questions.explanation: Do not use high beams when another vehicle is nearby. Switch to low beam to keep everyone safe on the road.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to slow down.
Do not drive in this lane.
You must stop completely and let others go first.
Slow down, be ready to stop, and let others pass if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, be ready to stop, and let others pass if needed.
questions.explanation: This triangular sign means you must yield. Slow down as you approach the intersection and be ready to stop. Let other vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians pass safely before you go.

questions.question: You are driving up a hill and see a heavy truck ahead. What should you know?

options.text: The truck may be going slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to pass the truck safely.
You may not be allowed to pass the truck.

questions.explanation: Large trucks often go slower than the speed limit, especially on hills. Be careful when approaching them. On hills with poor visibility, it is illegal to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop, then go when the way is clear.
Stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
You can turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must stop completely and stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears, unless a sign says otherwise.

questions.question: What should car drivers know about large trucks?

options.text: They can stop faster than cars.
They need the same amount of space as cars to maneuver.

questions.explanation: Large trucks have big blind spots in front, on the sides, and behind. Stay out of these areas. Trucks need more room to turn and stop than cars because of their size and weight.
